en.usage: Ages 12 and older and adults chew 2 tablets (1 g) at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes to 1 hour after meals. If needed, one more dose may be taken before bedtime. Follow the prescribed dosage.
en.caution: Do not take this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, have Alzheimer's disease, hemorrhoids, fluid retention (edema), toxemia of pregnancy, diarrhea, undiagnosed gastrointestinal bleeding, or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have kidney impairment, are physically weak, are on a low-phosphorus diet, have a digestion/absorption disorder, are elderly, have symptoms of gastrointestinal bleeding such as vomiting blood or black stools, or are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; if there is no improvement after about 2 weeks, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist. Follow the prescribed dosage. When giving to children, administer under the supervision of a guardian. Do not take with tetracycline antibiotics; consult a pharmacist when taking with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, ulcer treatments, digitalis preparations, chlorpromazine, lansoprazole, prednisolone, penicillin, quinolones, iron (Fe) salt preparations, or salicylates. Stop taking it and consult a pharmacist if constipation or diarrhea occurs.

en.title: Megatrue Focus Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for supplementation of vitamins A, D, B1, B2, B6, C during physical fatigue, pregnancy/lactation, reduced stamina during or after illness, growth periods, and old age; relief of dry eyes and night blindness; prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets; relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (low-back pain, stiff shoulders, etc.), beriberi, eye fatigue, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and supplementation of zinc.
en.usage: Ages 12 and older and adults take 1 tablet at a time, 1 to 2 times a day. Follow the prescribed dosage.
en.caution: Warning: taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A per day can cause birth defects; women within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take it. Do not take this medicine if you have hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, are hypersensitive to it, are an infant under 12 months, or have kidney stones or severe renal failure. Consult a pharmacist before use if you have hyperoxaluria, are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breastfeeding, are a premature infant or infant, have cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, kidney impairment, low blood protein, gout, kidney stones or a history thereof; if there is no improvement after about a month, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist. Follow the prescribed dosage. This medicine may turn the urine yellow and affect test values or interfere with glucose detection in urine tests. Do not take with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracyclines, antacids, or levodopa; consult a pharmacist when taking with cardiac glycosides, antialdosterone agents, or triamterene; avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before and after use. Stop taking it and consult a pharmacist if you develop nausea, vomiting, itching, dry rough skin, painful joint swelling, diarrhea, loose stools, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, cardiac arrest, central nervous system depression, gastrointestinal disorders, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, or pulmonary edema.
